column2: Czech Republic: government approves the strategy to introduce BIM
column3: With resolution no. 682 the Czech government approves the «Koncepce zavádění metody BIM», the ten-year plan to introduce BIM: standards, training and a mandate for large public works, later postponed and turned into the 2025 BIM law.

column2: Brazil: the national BIM strategy is born
column3: With Decree 9.377 the Brazilian government establishes the BIM BR Strategy to spread BIM in the country, with an inter-ministerial management committee. It is the starting point of the mandate in federal works that began in 2021.

column2: ISO 19650 is born: BIM has its international standard
column3: ISO publishes the first two parts of ISO 19650, concepts and principles and the delivery phase of assets: information management using BIM becomes an international standard, derived from the British standards BS 1192 and PAS 1192.

column2: Spain: inter-ministerial BIM commission set up
column3: Royal Decree 1515/2018 creates the Comisión Interministerial to introduce BIM in the State's public procurement: it will write the BIM Plan approved in 2023.

column2: UNI/TS 11337-3: digital product data sheets
column3: The UNI committee publishes technical specification 11337-3, the first piece of the Italian BIM series: a model for collecting, organising and storing the technical information of construction products, not only geometric data.

column2: ANAS announces its first BIM tender for early 2017
column3: ANAS, Italy's road agency, speeds up the introduction of BIM in tenders: the first tender is planned for early 2017 and the full switch to digital within three years, ahead of the decree that will set the mandate.

column2: OICE: BIM tenders more than tripled in one year
column3: According to OICE, the Italian association of engineering firms, in 2017 there were 86 public tenders requiring BIM, against 26 in 2016 and just 4 in 2015: still small numbers compared with all design tenders, but growing fast.

column2: Second OICE report: BIM tenders reach 11% of value
column3: In 2018, engineering and architecture service tenders requiring BIM were 4.6% of the total by number and 11.4% by value. The most active client is the State Property Agency with its regional offices.

column2: OICE: 560 BIM tenders in 2020, but few information requirements
column3: In 2020, tenders for design and technical services mentioning BIM numbered 560, 8.7% of the total; only 16.8% of them included information requirements. OICE points out that tenders are still very uneven.

column2: Austria: ÖNORM A 6241-2 for level 3 BIM
column3: Austrian Standards publishes the second part of ÖNORM A 6241, the Austrian BIM standard defining how to work on a shared, structured model (level 3, «iBIM»), with a common catalogue of object properties.

column2: Germany: BIM4INFRA2020 starts for federal pilot projects
column3: The transport ministry commissions a consortium of companies and universities to provide scientific support to BIM pilot projects on roads, railways and waterways, preparing the regular use of BIM in new federal works from 2020.

column2: Germany: «Masterplan Bauen 4.0» launches 20 new pilot projects
column3: Minister Dobrindt presents the Masterplan Bauen 4.0: 20 new BIM pilot projects on roads, railways and waterways, with €30 million, towards the regular use of BIM in federal projects from 2020.

column2: BIM4INFRA2020: recommendations for federal works
column3: The BIM4INFRA2020 consortium publishes operational recommendations for BIM in infrastructure: employer's information requirements, BIM execution plan and use cases, ahead of 2020, when all new transport ministry projects must use digital methods.

column2: France: the plan for the digital transition in construction starts
column3: Presented by minister Sylvia Pinel at the end of 2014, the PTNB (Plan Transition Numérique dans le Bâtiment) starts operating in January 2015, the 2015–2018 programme to spread BIM and digital tools across the construction sector.

column2: United Kingdom: the «Digital Built Britain» strategy for level 3 BIM
column3: The British government publishes the Digital Built Britain strategic plan to go beyond BIM Level 2: open data shared across the whole life of assets, smart cities and digital asset management.

column2: Spain: the es.BIM commission is set up
column3: The Ministry of Development (Fomento) sets up the commission to introduce BIM in the Spanish construction sector, later known as es.BIM: the first step on the path to the national BIM Plan.

column2: France: the sector signs the «Objectif BIM 2022» charter
column3: At the Batimat fair in Paris, the whole French construction sector signs the «Objectif BIM 2022» charter, a voluntary commitment to generalise BIM in new buildings by 2022.

column2: France: the government launches the BIM 2022 Plan
column3: The minister for cities and housing signs the BIM 2022 Plan with the construction sector, aiming to make BIM the norm for new buildings by 2022 and continuing the work of the PTNB.

column2: Chile: the national BIM standard for public works
column3: Planbim, Corfo's BIM programme, publishes the «Estándar BIM para Proyectos Públicos»: common vocabulary, coding and requirements for administrations requiring BIM, written with 34 public, private and academic organisations.

column2: Hong Kong: BIM becomes mandatory in public works
column3: With technical circular 7/2017, the Development Bureau makes BIM mandatory in public works projects above HK$30 million designed from 2018, in all stages from feasibility studies to construction.

column2: Japan: the Council for BIM in buildings meets for the first time
column3: The infrastructure ministry sets up the «Building BIM Promotion Council», a table between the public sector, private sector and universities to spread BIM in the design, construction and management of buildings: it will lead to national guidelines and, in 2026, design review with BIM.

column2: Japan: first national guidelines on the BIM workflow
column3: The ministry publishes the first edition of the guidelines on the standard BIM workflow for buildings, from design to construction and maintenance, with the roles of the different actors and ways to make use of the models.

column2: United States: third version of the national BIM standard released
column3: The buildingSMART alliance of the National Institute of Building Sciences publishes NBIMS-US version 3: more than 3,100 pages with COBie 2.4 and level of development specifications, free to download.

column2: Australia: national strategic framework for BIM approved
column3: The Board of Treasurers approves the «Australian BIM Strategic Framework», led by Victoria and Queensland with the Australasian BIM Advisory Board, to be applied in all states and territories to harmonise the use of BIM in major works and public buildings.

column2: Argentina: BIM plan for public works presented
column3: The Argentine government presents the SIBIM programme to introduce BIM in national public works, with the BIM strategy decrees and the creation of a BIM table at the Ministry of the Interior, Public Works and Housing.

column2: Peru: the BIM Plan for public investment is born
column3: With Supreme Decree 289-2019-EF the Peruvian government sets the rules to gradually introduce BIM in public investment, the first step of Plan BIM Perú led by the Ministry of Economy and Finance.

column2: Abu Dhabi adopts BIM for major projects
column3: Abu Dhabi's municipal department announces the adoption of BIM for the emirate's main construction projects, following the path opened by Dubai.

column2: Poland: roadmap to introduce BIM in public procurement
column3: As part of the project «Cyfryzacja procesu budowlanego w Polsce», the Ministry of Development publishes the «Mapa drogowa» for the gradual introduction of BIM in public procurement, prepared with the support of the European Commission. Poland does not yet have a general mandate.

column2: United Kingdom: the Gemini Principles for a national digital twin
column3: The Centre for Digital Built Britain publishes the Gemini Principles, nine principles (public good, value creation, insight, security, openness, quality, federation, curation, evolution) for building a «National Digital Twin»: an ecosystem of digital twins connected by securely shared data.

column2: Mexico: national strategy for BIM in public works
column3: The Mexican government, through the Investment Unit of the Ministry of Finance (SHCP), publishes the Strategy for the introduction of «Modelado de Información de la Construcción» (MIC), the official name of BIM in Mexico. The plan aims to adopt BIM in public works within eight years, to improve project quality, transparency and accountability.

column2: Costa Rica: towards a national BIM plan for public works
column3: Costa Rica's construction sector adopts BIM mainly in private projects; for public works, the Ministry of Planning (MIDEPLAN) is preparing a National BIM Implementation Plan, promoted by the office of the First Lady.

column2: Uruguay: third national BIM meeting and an inter-ministerial committee
column3: At the third national BIM meeting, organised by the National Development Corporation and the Chamber of Construction, the Uruguayan government confirms its interest in BIM for public works. The National BIM Committee brings together the ministries of Transport and Public Works, Economy and Housing, with other public bodies.

column2: Colombia: national BIM strategy, mandatory from 2026
column3: The National Planning Department (DNP) presents the BIM Adoption Strategy, built with the ministries of Housing and Transport: first pilot projects, then progressive adoption, up to a national BIM mandate in 2026, with the aim of applying it to 85% to 100% of public construction projects.

column2: Costa Rica: a bill to make BIM mandatory in public works
column3: Bill 24587, the «Framework Law on Information Management Technologies for Construction», is introduced in the Legislative Assembly; it would make BIM progressively mandatory in public works, for greater efficiency, transparency and control.

column2: Colombia: the Ministry of Transport adopts BIM
column3: With a resolution of 17 October 2024 the Ministry of Transport adopts BIM in the sector's infrastructure projects and creates the Mesa de Articulación Interinstitucional BIM (MAI-BIM), where national and territorial bodies coordinate implementation. Four BIM guides for transport projects have been prepared within the table.

column2: Bogotá: the Urban Development Institute's 2024–2027 BIM plan
column3: The IDU, the body that designs streets and public space in Bogotá, publishes its 2024–2027 BIM action plan. With the previous plan, by 2023 92% of newly awarded projects were already managed in BIM; now the goal is to measure time and costs and bring BIM into the whole life cycle of the works.

column2: Costa Rica: CFIA's first national BIM standard
column3: The Federated College of Engineers and Architects (CFIA) publishes the «Estándar BIM para proyectos en Costa Rica», version 1, presented at the BIM CON 2025 congress: a common reference for clients and professionals that adapts international standards and protocols to the national context.

column2: Peru: 50 public bodies already have a BIM plan
column3: The Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) announces that 50 public bodies and companies, including ministries, infrastructure programmes and regional governments, have approved their BIM implementation plan, ahead of the mandate from August 2026 for the defined project types.

column2: Peru: BIM mandatory in 14 types of public works
column3: The BIM mandate comes into force for investments by the national and regional governments in 14 types, including hospitals, universities, national and regional roads, transport systems, irrigation and police stations. It applies from the formulation and execution stages, depending on where each project stands.

column2: Ethiopia: towards mandatory BIM in large public works
column3: Public works above 250 million birr will have to use BIM, under a project led by the Construction Management Institute expected to start the following year. Meanwhile the Ethiopian Standards Institute prepares national guidelines and the Ministry of Urban and Infrastructure Development the complementary rules.

column2: South Africa: a national BIM framework in the construction summit declaration
column3: Public Works Minister Dean Macpherson and the provincial ministers adopt the 2025 National Construction Summit Declaration. Its commitments include a national BIM framework for the sector, to be published by the end of September 2026, together with the digitalisation of public project management.
